Polymarket and Kalshi now give Vivek only a 42% chance of winning the Ohio governor's race

Joel Abbott Sep 22, 2026
Ohio Vivek Ramaswamy 2026 Midterms
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:57
Instaread

It seems people haven't forgotten those comments about "Saved by the Bell."

As of Tuesday, the two leading gamble-on-everything sites have Vivek Ramaswamy at a 42% chance to win the Ohio governor's race.

Like any type of poll, these "prediction markets" should be taken with a bit of gambling salt.

While these betting sites have proven to be more accurate than oft-lopsided political polling, 42% odds means Vivek still wins 42 out of 100 possible scenarios.

Democrat Amy Acton is also facing problems in her own camp:

The story is not that Vivek has the possibility to lose, but that he ever got into such a dire position in a consistently "purple" red state.

The last Democrat was the one-term Ted Strickland, who was elected 20 years ago in 2006. Before that, it was Dick Celeste in 1983, a full generation prior.

While Democrats controlled the state house for most of the '70s to '90s, the legislature has largely been a GOP-majority throughout the state's history.

But Amy Acton is not the same Democrat of the 1970s. She is far more radical (see: her Covid policies as an advisor to Gov. DeWine) and will push a shift to the far left, like what has happened in Michigan and Virginia.

The leftward drift of the Democratic Party has solidified Ohio as a red state in the past 10-15 years. The legislature is a GOP supermajority, and that is unlikely to change. It is a state with a strong Christian family ethic; one that doesn't want to elect politicians who make everything fake and gay.

All of this makes Vivek's apparent underdog status a veritable surprise. Ohio should have been a slam dunk for the GOP. All they had to do was run a warm body with a kind face and a few pro-family, anti-woke slogans.

Instead...

Ohioans, chip in and let us know the mood on the ground!
